title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types

tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written for Teraminds Academy from the NCERT textbooks prescribed for 2026-27, modelled on the most-repeated question types in CBSE board papers 2023–26 and the Sample Question Paper 2026-27 (see our Board Blueprint). instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option.

patterns.T4: Interpret a historian's view or source

T1.name: Part I · Bricks, Beads and Bones (Harappa)
T1.tip: Mohenjodaro: citadel (Great Bath, warehouse) and lower town; planned drains laid out before houses. Chanhudaro: almost wholly craft production. Cunningham (first DG of ASI) used Chinese Buddhist pilgrims' accounts and missed Harappa's age; Marshall announced a new civilisation in 1924.
T1.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 1

T2.name: Part I · Kings, Farmers and Towns
T2.tip: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi and Kharosthi (1838). Most Ashokan inscriptions are in Prakrit; in the north-west, Aramaic and Greek. Punch-marked coins first; the Kushanas issued the first gold coins (c. 1st century CE).
T2.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 2

T3.name: Part I · Kinship, Caste and Class (Mahabharata)
T3.tip: Critical edition began 1919 under V.S. Sukthankar. Draupadi's marriage = polyandry. Brahmanical rule: a woman took her husband's gotra, but several Satavahana queens kept their fathers' gotra names (Gotami, Vasithi).
T3.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 3

T4.name: Part I · Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings (Buddhism, Jainism, Sanchi)
T4.tip: Tipitaka = Vinaya, Sutta and Abhidhamma Pitaka. Therigatha: verses by bhikkhunis. Sanchi survived thanks to the Begums of Bhopal (Shahjehan Begum, Sultan Jehan Begum).
T4.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 4

T5.name: Part II · Through the Eyes of Travellers
T5.tip: Al-Biruni: Kitab-ul-Hind in Arabic (11th c.), on caste and purity. Ibn Battuta: Rihla (14th c.), made qazi of Delhi by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Bernier (17th c.): thought the Mughal emperor owned all land (no private property).
T5.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 5

T6.name: Part II · Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
T6.tip: Alvars (Vishnu) and Nayanars (Shiva) in Tamil Nadu. Basavanna: Virashaiva (Lingayat) movement, Karnataka, 12th c. Sufis: khanqah (hospice), silsila (chain), sama (musical gatherings); Chishtis at Delhi (Nizamuddin Auliya) and Ajmer.
T6.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 6

T7.name: Part II · An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara
T7.tip: Founded 1336 by Harihara and Bukka. Colin Mackenzie mapped Hampi (1800). Amara-nayakas: military commanders given territories, paid tribute and supplied troops. Royal centre (Mahanavami dibba), sacred centre (Virupaksha, Vitthala).
T7.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 7

T8.name: Part II · Peasants, Zamindars and the State
T8.tip: Ain-i-Akbari by Abu'l Fazl (part of the Akbar Nama). Khud-kashta = resident peasants; pahi-kashta = non-resident cultivators. Jins-i-kamil ('perfect crops'): cash crops such as cotton and sugarcane.
T8.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 8

T9.name: Part III · Colonialism and the Countryside
T9.tip: Permanent Settlement 1793 (Cornwallis) in Bengal. Jotedars: rich peasants controlling land, trade and moneylending. Damin-i-Koh demarcated for the Santhals (1832). Fifth Report (1813) to the British Parliament.
T9.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 9

T10.name: Part III · Rebels and the Raj (1857)
T10.tip: Revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857; rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar their leader at Delhi. Awadh annexed in 1856. Rumours of cartridges greased with cow and pig fat.
T10.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 10

T11.name: Part III · Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
T11.tip: Champaran 1917 (indigo cultivators); Non-Cooperation 1920–22; Dandi/Salt March 1930; Quit India August 1942. Read sources (autobiography, letters, newspapers) critically: written after the event, for an audience.
T11.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 11

T12.name: Part III · Framing the Constitution
T12.tip: Constituent Assembly first met 9 December 1946; Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946; the Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950. G.B. Pant called separate electorates suicidal for minorities.
T12.ncert: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 12

MAP.name: Map work (5 marks)
MAP.tip: Practise the curriculum map list on an outline map: Harappan sites, Mahajanapadas and their capitals, Ashokan inscriptions, Vijayanagara, Mughal territories, centres of 1857 and of the national movement.
MAP.ncert: CBSE History curriculum 2026-27 map list (with Themes 1–2, 7, 10–11)

questions.question: The Great Bath was found in which part of Mohenjodaro?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath stood in the citadel along with structures like the warehouse.
questions.remediation: Part I · Bricks, Beads and Bones (Harappa): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 1; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Chanhudaro is significant because it was:
questions.explanation: Bead-making, shell-cutting, metal-working, seal-making and weight-making were done there.
questions.remediation: Part I · Bricks, Beads and Bones (Harappa): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 1; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: A port on the Red Sea
The capital of a Harappan king
A settlement devoted almost exclusively to craft production

questions.question: Why did Alexander Cunningham miss the significance of Harappa?
questions.explanation: His framework was early historic cities known from texts, so Harappan objects did not fit it.
questions.remediation: Part I · Bricks, Beads and Bones (Harappa): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 1; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: He used accounts of Chinese Buddhist pilgrims and tried to fit finds into the Early Historic period he knew
He thought the seals were Greek
He believed the site was a modern village

questions.question: Who deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in 1838?
questions.explanation: Prinsep, an officer in the mint of the East India Company, deciphered both.
questions.remediation: Part I · Kings, Farmers and Towns: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 2; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Most Ashokan inscriptions were in Prakrit. Those in the north-west of the subcontinent were in:
questions.explanation: Prakrit in Brahmi elsewhere; Aramaic and Greek (Kharosthi/Aramaic scripts) in the north-west.
questions.remediation: Part I · Kings, Farmers and Towns: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 2; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The first gold coins in the subcontinent were issued, c. first century CE, by the:
questions.explanation: Punch-marked silver and copper coins came first; the Kushanas issued the first gold coins.
questions.remediation: Part I · Kings, Farmers and Towns: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 2; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The project of preparing a critical edition of the Mahabharata began in 1919 under:
questions.explanation: Sukthankar led the team that compared manuscripts from across the subcontinent.
questions.remediation: Part I · Kinship, Caste and Class (Mahabharata): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 3; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Draupadi's marriage with the five Pandavas is an example of:
questions.explanation: Polyandry = a woman with several husbands; polygyny = a man with several wives.
questions.remediation: Part I · Kinship, Caste and Class (Mahabharata): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 3; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Several Satavahana queens are known by names derived from their fathers' gotras (such as Gotami). What does this suggest?
questions.explanation: The norm in Brahmanical texts was to take the husband's gotra; these names show it was not universally followed.
questions.remediation: Part I · Kinship, Caste and Class (Mahabharata): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 3; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Women had no names in Satavahana inscriptions
Not all women followed the Brahmanical rule of adopting the husband's gotra after marriage

questions.question: The Sanchi stupa survived largely because of the support of:
questions.explanation: The Begums of Bhopal funded its preservation.
questions.remediation: Part I · Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings (Buddhism, Jainism, Sanchi): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 4; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Shahjehan Begum and Sultan Jehan Begum, rulers of Bhopal
The rulers of the Vijayanagara empire

questions.question: The Tipitaka (three baskets) consists of the:
questions.explanation: Vinaya: rules for the Sangha; Sutta: the Buddha's teachings; Abhidhamma: philosophy.
questions.remediation: Part I · Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings (Buddhism, Jainism, Sanchi): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 4; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka and Abhidhamma Pitaka

questions.question: The Therigatha is unique because it is:
questions.explanation: It gives a rare insight into women's social and spiritual experiences.
questions.remediation: Part I · Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings (Buddhism, Jainism, Sanchi): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I (2026-27): Theme 4; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: A book of rules for kings
A collection of verses composed by bhikkhunis (Buddhist nuns)
The only Jaina text in Sanskrit

questions.question: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind was written in:
questions.explanation: Written in Arabic in the eleventh century.
questions.remediation: Part II · Through the Eyes of Travellers: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 5; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Ibn Battuta was appointed qazi (judge) of Delhi by:
questions.explanation: Impressed by his scholarship, Muhammad bin Tughlaq made him qazi of Delhi.
questions.remediation: Part II · Through the Eyes of Travellers: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 5; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: François Bernier argued that a major difference between Mughal India and Europe was that in India:
questions.explanation: Bernier saw crown ownership of land as harmful to the state and society; Mughal official documents do not show the state as the sole owner of land.
questions.remediation: Part II · Through the Eyes of Travellers: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 5; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: The emperor owned all the land, so there was no private property in land

questions.question: The Alvars and Nayanars were devotees of:
questions.explanation: Alvars: Vishnu; Nayanars: Shiva (Tamil Nadu, early bhakti).
questions.remediation: Part II · Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 6; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The Virashaiva (Lingayat) tradition in Karnataka was led by:
questions.explanation: Basavanna started the movement in Karnataka in the twelfth century.
questions.remediation: Part II · Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 6; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: In the Chishti tradition, sama refers to:
questions.explanation: Khanqah = hospice; silsila = chain; sama = music/audition in worship.
questions.remediation: Part II · Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 6; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: A tax paid to the state
The chain of succession from master to disciple
Musical gatherings with mystical chants, used to evoke divine ecstasy

questions.question: The Vijayanagara empire was founded in 1336 by:
questions.explanation: Two brothers, Harihara and Bukka, founded it in 1336.
questions.remediation: Part II · An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 7; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Who prepared the first survey map of the ruins at Hampi in 1800?
questions.explanation: Mackenzie, later the first Surveyor General of India, mapped Hampi.
questions.remediation: Part II · An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 7; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The amara-nayakas in the Vijayanagara empire were:
questions.explanation: They kept part of the revenue for themselves and their troops and sent tribute to the king.
questions.remediation: Part II · An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 7; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Priests in charge of the Virupaksha temple
Military commanders given territories to govern, who collected taxes and supplied troops to the king

questions.question: The Ain-i-Akbari was written by:
questions.explanation: It forms the third volume of the Akbar Nama.
questions.remediation: Part II · Peasants, Zamindars and the State: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 8; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: In Mughal records, khud-kashta peasants were:
questions.explanation: Khud-kashta: resident; pahi-kashta: non-resident cultivators.
questions.remediation: Part II · Peasants, Zamindars and the State: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 8; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Residents of the village where they held their lands

questions.question: Jins-i-kamil ('perfect crops') were crops such as:
questions.explanation: Cash crops earned more revenue for the state.
questions.remediation: Part II · Peasants, Zamindars and the State: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II (2026-27): Theme 8; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Millets grown only for the farmer's family
Rice grown only in temple lands
Cotton and sugarcane, which the state encouraged because they brought more revenue

questions.question: The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal in 1793 by:
questions.explanation: It fixed revenue permanently with zamindars.
questions.remediation: Part III · Colonialism and the Countryside: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 9; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: In late 18th-century Bengal, jotedars were:
questions.explanation: Their power in villages was often greater than that of the zamindars.
questions.remediation: Part III · Colonialism and the Countryside: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 9; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Rich peasants who controlled large areas of land, local trade and moneylending

questions.question: The area demarcated by the British in 1832 for the Santhals was called:
questions.explanation: The Santhals settled in the Damin-i-Koh around the Rajmahal hills.
questions.remediation: Part III · Colonialism and the Countryside: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 9; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The revolt of 1857 began with the uprising of sepoys at:
questions.explanation: The sepoys at Meerut mutinied on the afternoon of 10 May 1857 and then marched to Delhi.
questions.remediation: Part III · Rebels and the Raj (1857): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 10; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Awadh was annexed to the British empire in:
questions.explanation: Dalhousie annexed Awadh in 1856 on the ground of misgovernment.
questions.remediation: Part III · Rebels and the Raj (1857): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 10; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: At Delhi, the rebel sepoys of 1857 proclaimed as their leader:
questions.explanation: Using the Mughal emperor's name gave the revolt legitimacy.
questions.remediation: Part III · Rebels and the Raj (1857): NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 10; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: The Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar

questions.question: Gandhiji's 1917 movement in Champaran was on behalf of:
questions.explanation: He sought security of tenure and freedom to grow crops of choice for peasants.
questions.remediation: Part III · Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 11; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The Salt March to Dandi took place in:
questions.explanation: Gandhiji began the march in March 1930 and broke the salt law at Dandi.
questions.remediation: Part III · Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 11; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The Quit India movement was launched in:
questions.explanation: Launched in August 1942 after the failure of the Cripps Mission.
questions.remediation: Part III · Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 11; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Why must a historian read Gandhiji's autobiography critically?
questions.explanation: Autobiographies are reconstructions of the past; they need to be checked against other sources.
questions.remediation: Part III · Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 11; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: It is a retrospective account, written later from memory and shaped by what the author wanted to present
It was written before he was born
It contains no information about events
It was written by the British government

questions.question: The Constituent Assembly of India first met on:
questions.explanation: The first session was on 9 December 1946.
questions.remediation: Part III · Framing the Constitution: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 12; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Who moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946?
questions.explanation: Nehru's resolution set out the ideals of the Constitution.
questions.remediation: Part III · Framing the Constitution: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 12; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The Constitution of India came into effect on:
questions.explanation: It came into effect on 26 January 1950.
questions.remediation: Part III · Framing the Constitution: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 12; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true; his reason (R) explains his opposition (A).
questions.remediation: Part III · Framing the Constitution: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part III (2026-27): Theme 12; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
questions.assertion: Govind Ballabh Pant opposed separate electorates in the Constituent Assembly.
questions.reason: He argued that they would isolate the minorities permanently and were suicidal for them.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Which of these Harappan sites is in present-day Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Lothal (Gujarat); Kalibangan (Rajasthan); Banawali (Haryana); Harappa (Punjab, Pakistan).

questions.question: Rajagaha (Rajgir) was the capital of which mahajanapada?
questions.explanation: Rajagaha was Magadha's early capital; later the capital shifted to Pataliputra.
questions.remediation: Map work (5 marks): CBSE History curriculum 2026-27 map list (with Themes 1–2, 7, 10–11); then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
